answers.ui_testing: Headless Chromium via Playwright (pre-installed in the environment): render the real single-page app — Leaflet map included, with map tiles and other network faked deterministically — and assert pixel-exact visual goldens the owner reviews by sight; short per-leaf tests drive to a state and capture. Pure planner rules (plan/lib) stay node --test logic leaves. No visual harness exists yet — this is the target mechanism.
answers.requirements_source: Authored fresh at product/requirements.md (config.spec), distilled from the existing product brief docs/product-spec.md. No prior formal requirements doc or issue-tracker backlog to extract.

answers.hosting: GitHub Pages from this repo — confirmed from the repo rather than asked: the hand-rolled Pages workflow this adoption replaces already deployed to Pages on push to main via actions/deploy-pages, with no CNAME and no other host. So the full set is vendored: orchestrator + publish/deploy reusables + the three composite actions.
answers.publish_set: Rooted at the repo root. The site is the four pages (index, accessibility, privacy, terms), the favicons and .nojekyll, css/, js/, shared/, the planner's own paths (plan/index.html, plan/plan.css, plan/plan.js, plan/lib), package.json (the debug pill fetches it for the version), and only the data the browser actually fetches: data/venues.json, data/days/, and the three normalized sidecars the planner loads (shows.min.json, availability.min.json, descriptions.min.json). Derived from the fetch call sites in js/app.js and plan/plan.js, not from 'everything except the tooling'. Deliberately excluded: data/normalized/shows.json (7.4M) and data/prices.json (2.9M) are scraper-side inputs no page fetches, plus scraper/, docs/, design-concepts/, product-wiki/, plan/design/, scripts/ and the agent tooling.

answers.product: Fringe Discover: a spontaneity/reachability tool for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Where listings apps answer 'what exists?', this answers 'what can I actually make right now?' — given the user's location, how far they'll travel and how, and their next commitment, it collapses ~3,800 shows into a short list of genuinely reachable options that haven't started and still leave time to reach whatever is next.
answers.users: Fringe-goers mid-festival, usually on foot and without a fixed plan — visitors with a gap between a booked show and dinner, locals and tourists intimidated by the programme's scale. Decisive in the moment rather than researchers: they want a short list of good, reachable options, not 3,800 search results. Emotional target: 'delight + relief'.
answers.market: Edinburgh Fringe discovery and planning tools. Alternatives: the official Fringe app (a 'Nearby now' + shake-to-search finder), Plan My Fringe (a schedule optimiser with a walking-time 'Fringe Trail'), the edfringe.com programme and filters, the Half Price Hut (same-day discounts), review outlets such as ThreeWeeks, plus street posters and word-of-mouth. None centres full reachability — travel mode plus next-commitment slack — the way Fringe Discover does.

accept.reason: the executable-requirements layout is a framework contract: cases live in <kind>/cases/ and the harness in shared/, so every case's reach to shared/ and to the shipped modules under js/, plan/ and shared/ is fixed by the pack's layout standard, not a placement choice

the repo's one verification gate invokes the world sweep (engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs) so that passing it locally means what passing CI means — a commit that passed verify and went red on CI for a blocking conformance finding is what prompted this. Not the coupling the rule guards against: no canon internals are imported and nothing is inlined, it is the same documented CLI entry point .github/workflows/ already spells under the rule's own carve-out. A canon rename of that one path breaks the workflow and this script identically, and the fix is the same one line
